en: Jupiter is so massive that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside its total volume.
About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun, which is considered an average-sized star in the Milky Way galaxy.
The Moon is about 384,400 kilometers from Earth, meaning you could fit roughly 30 Earths side-by-side in the space between them.
On the Mohs hardness scale, talc is the softest mineral at number one, while diamond is the hardest at number ten.
Oceans hold about 97 percent of all Earth's water, leaving only three percent as freshwater for drinking and agriculture.
In 2013, Super Typhoon Haiyan struck the Philippines with sustained winds of 315 kilometers per hour, ranking among the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded.
The tallest tsunami wave ever recorded reached 524 meters in Lituya Bay, Alaska, in 1958, making it taller than the Empire State Building.
It takes nature approximately 500 years to form just one inch of fertile topsoil under normal agricultural conditions.
The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia is the deepest artificial point on Earth, reaching 12,262 meters straight down into the crust.
Neptune is so distant that it takes 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun, compared to Earth's single 365-day year.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California, in 1913.
Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted in 1815 with such massive force that it ejected 160 cubic kilometers of volcanic ash into the sky.
